memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Balak said to him, "Come with me to another place where you can see them; you will not see them all but only the outskirts of their camp. And from there, curse them for me." So he took him to the field of Zophim on the top of Pisgah, and there he built seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on each altar. - Num 23:13-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Balak refuses to give up. If the first location produced a blessing, perhaps a different vantage point will yield the curse he wants. He takes Balaam to a new place, builds seven more altars, and offers more sacrifices. Surely, he thinks, a change of scenery will change the outcome.

There is a strange logic to Balak's persistence. He believes the problem lies in the circumstances, the location, the ritual, rather than in his opposition to God. If he can just adjust the conditions, he imagines he can get the result he desires. He never stops to consider that he is fighting against God Himself.

We can fall into the same error. When we are set on a course God has not blessed, we sometimes keep changing our approach, trying new angles and strategies, rather than asking whether we are opposing God's will altogether. Persistence in the wrong direction is not virtue; it is stubbornness.

The wiser path is to stop and examine whether our desire aligns with God's revealed will. No change of location or method will make God bless what He has not blessed. In Christ, we are called to submit our plans to God rather than endlessly reshaping our schemes (Jas 4:15). Ask not merely how to succeed, but whether God is in it at all.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you keep changing your approach instead of asking whether God is in your plan?
2. When have you persisted in a direction God had not blessed?
3. How can you submit your plans to God's will rather than your own?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, keep me from stubbornly pursuing what You have not blessed. Teach me to examine my plans in the light of Your will and to submit my ways to You. Amen.
